extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office personnel, patent owners, and third‑party submitters/requesters (patent practitioners and agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for citing prior art and for filing, processing, and concluding ex parte reexamination requests and related submissions under 35 U.S.C. §§301–307 and 37 CFR §§1.501–1.502, 1.902, and related rules. Includes how submissions are to be formatted, what content is permitted, timing, confidentiality, service, and certificate formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may cite prior art or written statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person at any time may cite to the Office prior art consisting of patents or printed publications or written statements of the patent owner filed in a proceeding before a Federal court or the Office (35 U.S.C. 301).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Any person’ includes individuals, corporations, governmental entities, patentees, licensees, reexamination requesters, real parties in interest, persons without a real interest, and persons acting for real parties in interest. Patent examiners must not create such submissions on their own initiative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content limitation of 35 U.S.C. 301/37 CFR 1.501 submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions under 35 U.S.C. 301 and 37 CFR 1.501 are limited to patents, printed publications, and/or patent owner written claim‑scope statements (and accompanying additional information) and an explanation of their pertinence and manner of applying to at least one claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of all cited documents and necessary English translations must be included. Affidavits/declarations may accompany submissions to explain contents or pertinent dates (e.g., commercial success). Submissions cannot include issues not directed to patents/printed publications/written claim scope statements (for example, 35 U.S.C. 112 arguments, public use statements, conduct of the patent owner, or argument about references previously treated in prosecution or reexamination). If a submission contains such prohibited material it should not be entered and should be returned to the sender (see MPEP §2206).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation requirement (pertinence and manner of applying)
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission must include an explanation in writing of the pertinence and manner of applying any prior art or written statement to at least one claim of the patent for the submission to become part of the official file (35 U.S.C. 301(b); 37 CFR 1.501(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The explanation should set forth, for at least one claim, how each cited item shows or teaches at least one limitation of the claim. Patent owners may also include explanations of how the claims differ from submitted prior art. Examples in MPEP show claim‑by‑claim mapping and references to figures/col/lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required accompanying materials for written statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any statement submitted under 35 U.S.C. 301(a)(2) must be accompanied by any other documents, pleadings, or evidence from the proceeding in which the statement was filed that address the written statement (35 U.S.C. 301(c); 37 CFR 1.501(a)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions of written statements must identify the forum and proceeding, the specific papers and portions containing the statements, and how each statement is a position on claim scope (37 CFR 1.501(a)(3)). If a submitted written statement or additional information is subject to a protective order, the submission must be redacted to exclude protected information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions under 35 U.S.C. 301 may be filed at any time during the period of enforceability of the patent (defined as the patent term plus 6 years under 35 U.S.C. 286), and in some circumstances after expiration if litigation within the statute of limitations is instituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions filed after an order to reexamine will not be entered into the patent file until the reexamination is concluded (37 CFR 1.501(c)), except in specified circumstances (e.g., submitted by the patent owner; by an ex parte reexamination requester who also submits the fee and required documents; in an ex parte third party requester’s reply under 37 CFR 1.535; or as an enterable submission under 37 CFR 1.948 during inter partes reexamination). Presenting art before a reexamination is ordered ensures it may be considered without paying another reexamination fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of service requirement for third‑party submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission under 37 CFR 1.501 by a person other than the patent owner must include a certification that a copy of the submission was served in its entirety upon the patent owner at the correspondence address provided in §1.33(c) (37 CFR 1.501(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a third‑party submission fails to include proper proof of service as required by 37 CFR 1.248(b), it will not be entered into the patent file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of submitter identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon the written request of the person citing prior art or written statements, that person’s identity shall be excluded from the patent file and kept confidential (35 U.S.C. 301(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To maintain confidentiality, submissions should be submitted anonymously without identification. Submitters are advised not to identify themselves anywhere in their papers because complete assurance of exclusion from public files cannot be guaranteed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redaction requirement for protective orders
rubrics_metrics.description: If any written statement or additional information is subject to an applicable protective order, the statement or information shall be redacted to exclude information subject to that order (35 U.S.C. 301(d); 37 CFR 1.501(a)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the redacted version and include any permissible accompanying documents. Identify the portions removed and ensure the submission still satisfies the identification requirements of 37 CFR 1.501(a)(3) where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of patent on submission
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions should identify the patent to which the citation pertains by identifying the patent number, issue date, and patentee, preferably using a cover sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents themselves should also contain or have placed thereon an identification of the patent for which they are intended to facilitate processing and entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: What the submission must not include (prohibited content examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should not include issues not directed to patents, printed publications, or patent owner written claim scope statements and additional information—e.g., statements that claims violate 35 U.S.C. 112, statements about public use, or arguments about the conduct of the patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission includes prohibited material it should be returned to the sender and not entered into the patent file even if it otherwise contains acceptable patents/printed publications and explanations (see MPEP §2206).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable accompanying evidence (affidavits/declarations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits, declarations, or other written evidence relating to submitted documents may accompany a 37 CFR 1.501 submission to explain contents or pertinent dates in more detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include commercial success affidavits tied to a particular document, or declarations addressing enablement or dates. Such evidence must still be directed to the permitted scope of submissions and not introduce prohibited subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fee for 37 CFR 1.501 submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: No fee is required for the submission of citations under 37 CFR 1.501.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, strategic considerations exist: submitting art before reexamination is ordered avoids having to pay a reexamination fee to have the art considered in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and routing of submissions in the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions received under 37 CFR 1.501 are forwarded to the Technology Center (TC) that currently examines the class/subclass of the patent; the TC must promptly determine whether the submission meets statutory and regulatory requirements and enter it into the patent file if proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a proper submission is filed prior to an order in any pending reexamination it should be immediately entered into the reexamination file. If filed after an order and not entitled to entry under reexamination rules, the submission is retained (stored) in the TC until the reexamination is concluded (see 37 CFR 1.502 and 1.902). An e‑tag should be placed in the reexamination file history as a reminder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry timing for submissions vs reexamination status
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations submitted after the date of an order to reexamine by persons other than the patent owner or certain requesters will be delayed from entry into the patent file until the reexamination proceeding has been terminated (37 CFR 1.502, 1.902).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions where entry may occur sooner include citations by the patent owner, by an ex parte reexamination requester who also submits the fee and other required documents, in an ex parte third‑party requester’s reply under 37 CFR 1.535, or as an enterable submission under 37 CFR 1.948 during inter partes reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification when a proper submission is stored during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proper 37 CFR 1.501 submission is filed after an order for reexamination and is retained in storage until the reexamination is concluded, the patent owner and the third‑party submitter (if known) should be alerted by letter that the submission is being retained and will be placed in the patent file after conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification allows the patent owner to consider submitting art under 37 CFR 1.555 during reexamination and allows the submitter to consider filing a separate request for reexamination. If no duplicate copy was served on the patent owner, make the original available for copying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of improper submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a 37 CFR 1.501 submission is not proper (not limited to allowable items, lacks required description/information, or lacks proof of service), it will not be entered into the patent file; the third‑party submitter (if known) and the patent owner may be notified and the submission returned (MPEP §2206).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and form letters are provided in the MPEP. The Office may indicate the reason (e.g., inclusion of prohibited subject matter, missing proof of service) and provide direction for re‑submission if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification requirements for section 301 written statements
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission that includes section 301 written statements must identify (1) the forum and proceeding where the patent owner filed each statement, (2) the specific papers and portions containing the statements, and (3) how each statement is one in which the patent owner took a position on the scope of any claim in the patent (37 CFR 1.501(a)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification of portions can be satisfied by citing documents and specific page numbers. Provide information about the status of the proceeding and the relationship of the proceeding to the patent to assist the Office in identifying the claim scope statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A 37 CFR 1.501 submission by a person other than the patent owner must include proper proof of service; failing to include proper proof of service will result in the submission not being entered into the patent file (37 CFR 1.501(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof must reflect that a copy was mailed to or otherwise served upon the patent owner at the correspondence address in §1.33(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office consideration limits for written statements
rubrics_metrics.description: A written statement submitted under 35 U.S.C. 301(a)(2), and the additional information under 301(c), shall not be considered by the Office for any purpose other than to determine the proper meaning of a patent claim in a proceeding ordered or instituted pursuant to sections 304, 314, or 324 (35 U.S.C. 301(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits how such statements and accompanying documents may influence Office activity—generally restricted to claim construction in ordered proceedings. Protective‑order redactions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples and formatting of acceptable submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP provides sample submission letters (Example I: third party; Example II: patent owner) that show how to list references, map references to specific claims and patent figures/columns/lines, and include a certificate of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow examples for structure: identify patent, list references with bibliographic info, explain pertinence to specific claims with citations to figures/cols/lines, sign the submission, and include certificate of service when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of prior art in reexamination proceedings (entry rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations by the patent owner under §1.555 and by an ex parte reexamination requester under §§1.510 or 1.535 will be entered in the reexamination file. Citations submitted after the date of an order to reexamine by others will be delayed until termination of the reexamination (37 CFR 1.502).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.502 and 1.902 for processing rules during ex parte and inter partes reexamination proceedings. Place e‑tags and store materials in TC Rule 501 submission storage files as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination certificate formatting and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The ex parte reexamination certificate is titled 'Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate' with an ordinal number; the certificate number is the original patent number plus a two‑character kind code suffix (first letter B or C, second letter the reexamination iteration). The certificate indicates the date issued, bibliographic data, and a list of prior art available via PAIR, and identifies claims confirmed, canceled, disclaimed, or not examined. New claims are printed in italics; amended claims show italics and bracketing for amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inter partes and ex parte certificates use separate ordinal sequences. The certificate will print the text of new/amended claims and reference any prior court decisions. Follow MPEP §2287 and §901.04(a) for full formatting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervening rights for amended/new claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed amended or new claim determined to be patentable and incorporated into a patent following reexamination will have the same effect as specified in 35 U.S.C. 252 for reissued patents with respect to intervening rights (35 U.S.C. 307(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This means rights of persons who made, purchased, used, imported, or substantially prepared for the patented subject matter prior to issuance of the reexamination certificate are governed similarly to reissue intervening rights; see cited case law in MPEP for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination of a reexamination (how to consider claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for reexamination filed on a patent for which a reexamination certificate has already issued (a 'reexamination of a reexamination') must be considered based on the claims in the patent as modified by the previously issued reexamination certificate, not the original claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRU support staff must incorporate certificate changes into the reexamination specification before forwarding to the examiner. Examiners should verify the certificate changes are properly entered. Checklists (PTO‑1516, PTO‑1517) and supervisory reviews are required to ensure compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on patent owner amendments in reexamination of a reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to claims/specification must treat the reexamination certificate changes as part of the original patent; re‑adding text already in the certificate (e.g., italicized text) as if newly added is improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improper amendments will be treated as informal submissions; examiners should notify patent owner of defects (Form PTOL‑475) and set a one‑month period for correction. See MPEP §2266.02 for procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory forms for ex parte reexamination processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific USPTO forms must be used in ex parte reexamination actions and processing (e.g., PTOL‑471 Order Granting/Denying Request, PTOL‑466 Office Action, PTOL‑469 Notice of Intent to Issue Certificate, PTOL‑476 Reasons for Patentability/Confirmation, PTOL‑1516 Examiner Checklist, PTOL‑1517 Reexamination Clerk Checklist, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Request for Ex Parte Reexamination Transmittal Form PTO/SB/57 is available (not mandatory). Use the listed PTOL forms where required by MPEP procedures.
